newsitem.title: NIGERIA: NIGERIAN SHARES FALL FURTHER ON BEARISH SENTIMENT.
newsitem.headline: NIGERIAN SHARES FALL FURTHER ON BEARISH SENTIMENT.

text.p: Nigerian shares continued their downward path on Thursday although insurance companies and textiles defied the bearish trend to make small gains, dealers said.
The all-share index closed at 8012.22 from 8061.92 on Wednesday.
Traders said blue chip stocks continued to drop, with a large volume flooding the market given the gloomy economic outlook.
Lever Brothers and PZ Industries dropped 60 kobo apiece, both closing at 23.00 naira. UAC fell 10 kobo to 13.40 naira.
Nigerian Bottling Company finished 50 kobo down at 49.00 naira. Cadbury lost 40 kobo to 32.50 naira while Nestle and Northen Nigerian Flour Mills were each 10 kobo down at 50.40 naira and 8.50 naira.
Poor corporate showings recently ensured oil marketers' shares were further weakened on Thursday.
Unipetrol closed at 62.50 naira, National Oil at 49.50 naira and Total at 54.40 naira. All were 40 kobo down.
But impressive first quarter results at AIICO Insurance, following an equally good full year account, has turned its shares to the market's most sought after.
On Thursday, it appreciated 50 kobo to 17.00 naira.
Niger Insurance chalked up five kobo at 2.75 naira as the insurance sector continued to receive more attention.
United Nigerian Textiles was 10 kobo stronger at 6.20 naira and Afprint climbed three kobo to 2.66 naira on positive perception.
